extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent holders, and patent practitioners interacting with the Finnish Patent Office (PRH)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/ substantive standards used by the Finnish Patent Office (PRH) for handling patent prosecution (publication, grant, abandonment, reinstatement, abstracts, fee rules) and post-grant oppositions (väite). Covers timelines, formal requirements, allowable amendments, language and evidence rules, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment to broaden patent protection after PatL 19 notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be amended so that the patent protection is extended after a PatL 19 § notification has been given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: after the PatL 19 § notification new divisional applications cannot be filed by splitting (PatA 22 and 23 §). The purpose is to prevent changes that unnecessarily prolong grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRH issues PatL 19 notification only when publication-ready documents available
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH gives the PatL 19 § notification only when publication‑suitable documents relating to the application are available to PRH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the publication/acceptance process proceeds only when material for the patent publication exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restriction for national PCT continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: For a national application continued from a PCT application, notice of acceptance cannot be given before four months have elapsed after the end of the 31‑month period under PatL 31 § 1, unless the applicant agrees (PatL 34 §, PatA 52 b §).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to prevent premature acceptance for PCT‑derived national entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee payment obligation and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of the PatL 19 § notification the applicant is asked to pay the patent publication fee within two months. If the fee is not paid within the time limit, the application is left as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amount depends on whether documents were submitted on paper or electronically. Payment within the two months is the only mandatory obligation presented in the notice (failure leads to F.9 outcome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of publication fee for inventor‑applicant in hardship
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventor is the applicant, they may request exemption from the publication fee if paying would cause significant hardship (PatL 19 §). A statement of financial circumstances must accompany the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no supporting evidence is provided PRH requests tax/social authority statements. If the waiver request is rejected, a payment made within two months of rejection is considered timely for the original deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to defer grant until 18 months (postponement of grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting of the patent can be deferred only where granting would occur before the application becomes public under PatL 22 §, i.e., within 18 months of filing or priority date. The applicant may request deferral until the expiration of 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must request deferral and pay the publication fee within two months of the PatL 19 § notification for the deferral to be accepted (PatM 51 §). PRH sends confirmation of deferral only after fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRH decision to accept/grant subject to absence of new obstacles after PatL 19 notice
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH decides on acceptance of the application provided no new obstacle to acceptance has arisen after the PatL 19 § notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of obstacles: third‑party claim to a better right (PatL 18 §), or a cited publication brought up in a reminder/objection showing lack of novelty or lack of inventive step. Acceptance is withheld until such matters are finally resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRH will not decide acceptance before 12 months from filing/priority
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH will not make a decision to accept the application before 12 months have elapsed from the filing date or the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows intervening patent applications (published after filing) to be used as evidence in potential disputes (see E.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRH waits expiry of applicant's deferral period before deciding grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the applicant can request postponement within two months after the PatL 19 § notice, PRH does not decide on acceptance before that two‑month period has expired if the application is not yet public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant wants an earlier decision, they must explicitly request it and state they will not seek postponement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of patent publication before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Before deciding to accept/grant, PRH must prepare the patent publication (PatL 21 §) because the patent publication must be publicly available on the grant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH prepares the publication as soon as possible after the applicant has paid the publication fee or has been granted a waiver (PatA 31 §). PRH will not prepare the publication if an annual fee payment due date has passed unpaid; preparation awaits payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent deemed granted on Patent Gazette announcement day
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH publishes acceptance in the Patent Gazette; the patent is considered granted on the day the acceptance is announced (PatL 20 §).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent certificate is sent in paper if requested; it is also available via the patent information service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine‑month post‑grant opposition (väite) window
rubrics_metrics.description: Within nine months of the patent grant date any person may file an opposition (väite) against the granted patent (väiteaika).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition proceedings may result in revocation, dismissal, or maintenance of the patent in amended form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for opposition (PatL 25 § 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for an opposition are: (1) the patent was granted despite failure to meet PatL §§ 1, 1a, 1b, or 2; (2) the patent does not disclose the invention sufficiently for a skilled person to use it; (3) the patent contains subject‑matter that did not emerge from the application as filed (added matter); (4) the patent protection was extended after the PatL 19 § notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grounds differ from grant‑phase requirements: vague claim wording in granted claims is not per se a ground if the description enables the skilled person (cf. PatL 8 § 2 mom.). Lack of unity (PatL 10 §) is also not a ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal contents required in an opposition (PatA 33 §)
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition must state: (1) the opponent's name and address; (2) the patent registration number, patentee's name and invention title; (3) whether revocation or limitation is sought; (4) which of PatL 25 § 1 points the opposition is based on and any other facts supporting it; (5) if represented, the representative's name, domicile and address. Power of attorney must be shown if an agent represents the opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescribed fee must be paid for the opposition (PatL 24 § 1 mom.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination checklist and absolute vs discretionary defects (PatA 34 §)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH checks whether the opposition meets requirements within the opposition period and other statutory requirements. Absolute defects (must be corrected): missing fee; missing power of attorney for representative; failure to state whether revocation or limitation is sought; opposition not in Finnish/Swedish. Discretionary defects (PRH may require correction): missing translations for certain languages; insufficiently specified passages in supporting publications; not all supporting publications provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute (1–4) defects must be corrected without exception. Discretionary (5–7) defects may be requested for correction per the examining engineer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑admittance of opposition with uncorrected absolute defects
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition that does not meet the absolute requirements after the opposition period is not taken into substantive examination; PRH issues a reasoned decision which the opponent may appeal to the Market Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple oppositions exist and at least one is admitted for examination, all opposition material is considered but correspondence is exchanged only with those whose oppositions are taken up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of written statements in opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the patentee and opponents have the opportunity to submit written statements; PRH circulates relevant opposition documents and statements among the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH does not assess substantive arguments during ordinary correspondence other than to decide whether to continue correspondence or arrange an oral hearing. PRH may send extra statements where necessary (PatA 35 §).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to claims during opposition: no new matter, no broadening
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes made to a granted patent during opposition must not introduce subject matter that did not appear in the application as filed, nor may the patent protection be broadened as compared to the state after the PatL 19 § notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection broadens if a feature is removed entirely from a claim; it is allowed to replace the removed feature with a narrower feature taken from the description (permitted). Removing alternative features is allowed without broadening. Category changes (e.g., from method to product) can risk broadening; converting a product claim to a use claim for achieving a particular effect is generally acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added subject‑matter / new matter evaluation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposition phase evaluates added subject‑matter only with respect to whether features introduced in amended claims arise from the description or drawings; imprecision of granted independent claims is not itself a ground unless new features are imported from the description or figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If independent claims are amended based on dependent claims, the clarity of the amended claims is not re‑examined in certain MAO precedents (examples referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing rules in opposition (suullinen kuuleminen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearing is based on good administrative practice and may be held to allow parties to clarify written materials when necessary and when written procedure would produce unreasonable difficulty. Either patentee or opponent may request a hearing; the request must be justified and explain why certain material needs oral clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests cannot be conditional and cannot be justified solely by possibility of an unfavorable outcome. PRH decides necessity, invites all parties, issues an agenda, and covers listed points in one hearing. Hearing is not public; experts can attend but witnesses (e.g., for public use) cannot be heard. PRH gives no decision at the hearing and does not act as a court; it may, however, raise questions or views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation provisions in opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition and its reasoning must be submitted in Finnish or Swedish (PatM 52 §). Annexes may be in other languages. If supporting publications are in a language outside the listed set (fi/sv/no/da/en/de/fr), PRH may require translations of those publications if relevant to decision‑making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH sends procedural communications in Finnish or Swedish depending on the language used during examination. When the application was processed in English, claim language translations rules apply (see handling of English specification translations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party reminders (muistutus) during prosecution must be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: During prosecution PRH must consider all matters relevant to patentability. Any person may submit a reminder (third‑party observation) that brings prior publications or facts to PRH’s attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH notifies the applicant of such reminders and investigates whether the submitted material undermines patentability; PRH issues a reasoned statement on the significance. If a reminder arrives after an approving decision or PatL 19 notice, PRH issues a new communication only if the reminder creates an obstacle to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaving application as such (abandonment) grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is to be left as such if the applicant fails within a time limit to reply to an office action or to take measures to remedy noted deficiencies (PatL 15 §). Also if the applicant fails to pay the publication fee after PatL 19 notice or fails to pay annual fees, the application is left as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving as such terminates pendency. Some abandonments (e.g., for failure to respond to an office action or publication fee) may be reopened under conditions; abandonment due to unpaid annual fee is irreversible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening (taking application back into processing) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application was left as such because the applicant failed to respond to an office action or failed to pay the publication fee, the applicant may request that the application be taken up again by: (1) filing the omitted reply or correcting deficiencies or (2) paying the publication fee. Additionally a fee for re‑taking into processing must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific action (e.g., filing a reply, paying fee, or paying the reprocessing fee) is construed as a request; explicit request is recommended. PRH decides immediately upon such a request but will not make a negative decision before the four‑month period for making the request has elapsed. If the re‑take request is late or incomplete PRH may issue a reasoned rejection (appealable). If the request is not made in time, the application remains finally abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for public availability upon abandonment, reinstatement or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules govern when abandoned, reinstated, or appealed applications become public: e.g., if an application was abandoned before public disclosure and no appeal is filed, documents remain non‑public; if appeal is filed after abandonment but on/after the 18‑month publication date, documents become public on the appeal filing day; if reinstatement request is filed after 18 months from filing, documents become public on the day the request is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timing of requests for re‑examination or appeals affects the publication date; PRH provides examples showing when public availability results from different procedural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative correction/removal of a defective decision (hallintolaki 50 §)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Act (hallintolaki 50 §) PRH may remove/correct a decision if: (1) it is based on clearly erroneous or incomplete facts; (2) it is based on manifestly wrong application of law; (3) a procedural error occurred; or (4) new evidence has emerged that can materially affect the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction to the detriment of a party requires that party's consent unless the error is obvious and caused by the party's own conduct. Requests or initiatives for correction must be made within five years of the decision (hallintolaki 52 §). Correction requires re‑consideration and issuance of a new decision; certain limitations on appeal and notification to the Market Court apply (hallintolaki 53 §). PRH may e.g. remove an abandonment decision given on an incomplete basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (tiivistelmä) checking rules for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application becomes public, PRH prepares the application publication whose front page includes an abstract in two languages. PRH checks the substantive content and translation of the abstract; if noncompliant the applicant is asked to correct defects. PRH may itself make small necessary changes to the abstract without hearing the applicant (PatL 15 § 1 mom.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH also decides which drawings to publish with the abstract (PatM 27 §). The final abstract should, if possible, be confirmed before publication and must describe the invention as in the main application document; the abstract is not re‑examined/rewritten later due to claim changes or prosecution developments.
